title: Epistola Canonica: On those who ate meat sacrificed to idols during the barbarian invasion
pass_a_gloss: Epistola Canonica (Canonical Epistle). Gregory Thaumaturgus addresses those who, during the barbarian invasion, ate meat sacrificed to idols or committed other sins under duress. The epistle provides canonical penance for such cases. Gregory writes to a fellow bishop (canonical epistle). The epistle deals with penance for those who ate meat sacrificed to idols during the Gothic invasion, and other sins committed under compulsion. It establishes canonical penances based on the degree of voluntariness. Zonaras also comments on this epistle. The epistle was accepted at the Sixth Ecumenical Council.
notes_covered: Addresses penance for eating idol-meat during Gothic invasion
